page_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship

sources.entry: 📖 Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship, Robert C. Martin. Describes numerous useful best practices. A bit long. There's also a clean code cheatsheet.

summary.title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
summary.one_liner: Robert C. Martin's book on writing readable, maintainable code, covering naming, functions, objects, formatting, error handling, and unit testing, with refactoring case studies and a heuristics list.
keywords: how to tell good code from bad code
takeaways: Good names, small single-purpose functions, and few arguments make code easier to read and change.
Single Responsibility Principle: a class or module should have one reason to change.
Case studies show step-by-step refactoring of messy code into cleaner code.
A final chapter collects heuristics and code smells gathered from the case studies.
Reviewers note the examples are Java-centric and the printed code samples are hard to follow without an editor.
summary.summary: The book argues that poorly written code wastes large amounts of development time and presents practices for writing clean code as part of an agile software craftsmanship mindset. It is in three parts: principles, patterns and practices for clean code; several case studies of increasing complexity where code is refactored from problematic to sound; and a closing chapter of heuristics and smells. Topics listed include naming, functions, objects and classes, formatting, error handling, and unit testing with TDD. Reader reviews mention that the examples are heavily Java-specific and that printed code is harder to follow than code in an IDE.
